_meta.note: Structural regression golden. main-de-truncation-guard: the 12-section schema truncated at max_tokens 4000 in German → fixed with max_tokens 6000 + caps (response_strategies 3-4, what_NOT_to_say 3-4). 10 annotations stripped (glued onto response_text/tactic fields). PF-26 fixed. manipulation_tactics + draft_analysis.tone_flags/problematic_phrases neutralized to [] (interpretation-dependent). Re-locked 2026-08-23 (v2): adopted PF-39 v2 WITH an enforcement profile (router.outputGuard), and the schema lost everything the guard forbids — emotional_temperature, primary_emotion_detected, underlying_need, communication_style, the whole manipulation_tactics array, and draft_analysis.escalation_risk.level. A guard that fights its own schema on every call is not enforcement, it is a repair loop. message_analysis is now triggers_identified (quoted phrases only) plus whats_being_asked. cooling_recommendation.delay_time is words, not minutes. The follow-up endpoint no longer passes temperature/emotion/tactics as context. Guard verified firing live: 3 fields flagged and repaired on the first real input (predicted_recipient_reaction, emotion_inference_as_fact, unsupported_timing_rule). Re-locked 2026-08-23 (v3): second schema pass. what_this_does and risks removed from every strategy (an effect and a risk are both predictions about a stranger), and apology_assessment, what_NOT_to_say, timing_landmines, channel_landmines, if_they_continue_escalating and repair_strategy_later deleted whole — they were where the remaining mind-reading and unsupported prescriptions lived. Output is now a grounded read, 3-4 ready-to-send responses, and the follow-up Q&A. triggers_identified may carry a note about the WORDS as a possibility, never a determination about the sender. Both inline copy buttons removed. Re-locked 2026-08-23 (v4): the guard was checking every field EXCEPT the replies — the wiring named response_strategies[i].message and the schema field is response_text, so getByPath returned undefined and every reply was filtered out before the check ran. Also added contradicted_supplied_fact to the V2 checks: told the relationship was Partner, the output called them a roommate, which is a swap rather than an invention and nothing was looking for it. Prompt now pins the supplied relationship word and requires replies to reflect what was SAID, never what is FELT. Re-locked 2026-08-23 (v5): the repair pass was told it could return an empty string rather than filler, and did — a promised response option came back as "". outputGuard now takes requiredNonEmpty and restores the pre-repair value for any deliverable the repair hollowed out; a flawed reply the visitor can edit beats an empty box. Guard terms added: interpretation_as_fact, invented_relationship_dynamic, attitude_label. Check 4 now names attitude verdicts (contempt, disdain, dismissiveness, passive aggression) and "likely meaning" explicitly. Strategy labels must describe the reply, not what it avoids — "holds space without chasing" invented a chasing dynamic. Also a shape guard: response_strategies came back once as a STRING of Python-style pseudo-JSON, which the frontend maps over. Re-locked 2026-08-23 (v6): the prompt was replaced wholesale, and the output is now two keys — message_read and strategies[4]{title,tone,response_text}. goal_reality_check, draft_analysis, cooling_recommendation and message_analysis are gone; the two-call read/respond split went with them, since there is one small schema now. The guard collapsed to four tests: is it addressed to the other person, is it sendable as written, does it pursue the selected goal, does it avoid unsupported facts. Titles are checked as well as replies — "redirect without chasing" invents a dynamic and is the visitor-facing label. Follow-up Coaching and Adjust Tone remain as UI functionality against their own endpoints, not as generated analysis. Re-locked 2026-08-23 (v7): message_read must DESCRIBE the sentence, not classify it — offering "contempt, passive aggression, or frustrated venting" is three diagnoses rather than none. And a reply may speak for the VISITOR, never for the sender: "that felt like a dig" is theirs, "rather than an attempt to actually talk" assigns intent; "something has been bothering you" asserts a state nobody reported. Guard terms added: assigns_intent_to_sender, asserts_sender_state, classifies_rather_than_describes.

input.receivedMessage: You never listen to me. After everything I have done for you, you cannot even show up on time. I guess I am just not important to you.
input.userDraft: Wow you are being so dramatic right now, I was literally 10 minutes late
input.actualGoal: I want them to understand I care but also stop the guilt trips

output.message_read: 'You never listen to me' and 'I guess I am just not important to you' are both absolute claims that do not name a specific behaviour beyond being late — they frame a single incident as evidence of a pattern and a character conclusion. 'After everything I have done for you' adds a ledger framing without specifying what is owed. Together these phrases make it hard to respond to just the lateness, because the message has already expanded the scope. The tempted reply — calling it 'dramatic' and leading with 'literally 10 minutes late' — matches the escalation rather than addressing either the specific complaint or the bigger claim, which is likely to extend the argument rather than settle it.

strategies.title: Acknowledge the feeling, name the pattern you want to break
strategies.response_text: I can hear that you're really hurt, and I don't want to brush that off. Being late wasn't okay, and I'm sorry for that. I do want to say, though, that when it gets framed as me not caring about you at all, that's hard for me to sit with, because it's not true. I want us to be able to talk about the actual thing that happened without it becoming a verdict on whether I care. Can we do that?

strategies.title: Own the specific thing, gently push back on the larger claim
strategies.response_text: I was late, and that was wrong — I should have communicated better and I'm sorry. But 'I am just not important to you' — I don't think that's a fair read of who I am to you. I want to fix what actually happened today. I don't want to keep having a fight about whether I care, because I do. Let's talk about the lateness.

strategies.title: Name what the conversation is doing and redirect it
strategies.response_text: I hear that you're upset, and I take being late seriously. I want to talk about it. What I'm finding difficult is that the conversation has moved from me being late to me not caring about you at all — and I don't know how to respond to that in a way that actually helps us. I'm not dismissing what you feel. I just want us to talk about what happened rather than where that means we stand.

strategies.title: Short, low-temperature, opens the door
strategies.response_text: Being late wasn't okay and I'm sorry. I do care about you — I want you to know that isn't in question for me. When you're ready, I'd like to actually talk through what happened today, because I don't want to leave it here like this.

input.receivedMessage: Du hörst mir nie zu. Nach allem, was ich für dich getan habe, kannst du nicht einmal pünktlich sein. Ich schätze, ich bin dir einfach nicht wichtig.
input.userDraft: Wow, du bist gerade so dramatisch, ich war buchstäblich 10 Minuten zu spät
input.actualGoal: Ich möchte, dass sie verstehen, dass ich mich sorge, aber auch die Schuldgefühle stoppen

output.message_read: Die Nachricht enthält drei sehr unterschiedliche Aussagen, die zusammen Druck aufbauen. 'Du hörst mir nie zu' ist eine absolute Behauptung ohne konkretes Beispiel — sie lässt offen, was genau gemeint ist. 'Nach allem, was ich für dich getan habe' ruft eine unbenannte Schuld ab, ohne sie zu benennen. 'Ich schätze, ich bin dir einfach nicht wichtig' ist eine Aussage darüber, wie sich der Partner fühlt — nicht über eine bestimmte Handlung von dir.

strategies.title: Sorge zeigen, ohne die Schuld zu übernehmen
strategies.response_text: Du bist mir wichtig — das möchte ich gerade klar sagen. Ich war zu spät und das tut mir leid. Gleichzeitig möchte ich verstehen, was sich dahinter steckt. Der Satz 'ich bin dir nicht wichtig' stimmt nicht. Können wir kurz miteinander reden?

strategies.title: Konkretes anerkennen, weiten Vorwurf sanft ansprechen
strategies.response_text: Ja, ich war zu spät — das war nicht fair dir gegenüber, und das nehme ich ernst. Wenn du sagst, ich höre dir nie zu, würde ich gerne wissen, wann sich das so angefühlt hat, weil mir das wirklich wichtig ist. Ich möchte das nicht einfach stehen lassen.

strategies.title: Gefühl benennen, ohne Gegenangriff
strategies.response_text: Die Verspätung war von mir falsch — das erkenne ich an. Ich tue mich aber schwer mit dem Satz 'du bist mir nicht wichtig' — das stimmt einfach nicht, und ich möchte, dass du das weißt. Magst du mir sagen, was gerade wirklich los ist?

strategies.title: Kurz und offen — Gespräch einladen
strategies.response_text: Ich war zu spät, das tut mir leid. Und ich merke, dass da mehr dahintersteckt als die zehn Minuten. Ich bin da — reden wir, wenn du möchtest.
